headline: ArianeGroup completes Prometheus hot-fire test as Europe's committee vote nears
summary: ArianeGroup said on the sixth of November that its Prometheus reusable engine reached a new milestone in a hot-fire test in Germany.
Arianespace has set the next Ariane 6 flight, with 36 Amazon Leo satellites, for the twenty-third of November at the earliest.
The committee vote on a European-led orbital outpost is on the tenth of November, with Rome on the fifteenth of December.
Telesat has pushed full Lightspeed service in Canada to mid-2028, and KT SAT will lead a South Korean maritime connectivity project.
NASA's Swift observatory has been reported down over Indonesia, but NASA has published no page.
bottom_line: The road to Rome stands at the committee vote, with no new Council decision on file. The next date that matters is the tenth of November.

global.title: NASA holds the eighth of December date for commercial station proposals
global.summary: Artemis dates are unchanged. Commercial station proposals remain due on the eighth of December.
global.why: The station proposals are the next dated NASA decision point. No new NASA date, crew change or lander milestone is on file.

global.title: Blue Origin has not confirmed a January return for New Glenn
global.summary: A January 2027 return was reported earlier in the week and the company has not confirmed it. The FAA comment deadline of the thirtieth of October passed with no decision on file.
global.why: A company confirmation or an FAA decision would move this pathway. Neither is on file.
global.bar: Standing item; no fresh source in this reading.

global.why: Commercial relay providers are taking on a role in NASA communications. The packet gives no contract values.

audio_script:
Good morning. It is Sunday, the eighth of November, and this is the Sovereign Space ATLAS briefing. Europe's Prometheus reusable engine has completed a hot-fire test in Germany. NASA's Swift observatory has been reported down over Indonesia. And South Korea's KT SAT has been named to lead a maritime connectivity project.

Europe's reusable launcher work has a new test result and a dated flight. On the sixth of November, ArianeGroup said its Prometheus reusable rocket engine reached a new development milestone in a hot-fire test on the German Aerospace Center's P5 test bench. Arianespace has set the tenth Ariane 6 flight, carrying 36 Amazon Leo satellites, for the twenty-third of November at the earliest. That is the next date that matters for the launcher pathway. It falls before the Rome meeting on the fifteenth of December.

In Europe, the road to Rome continues. ESA announced on the third of November studies of a potential European-led orbital outpost in low Earth orbit. The studies feed the Rome decision. The committee vote is on the tenth of November. Rome follows on the fifteenth of December. No new Council decision is on file.

In Romania, Airbus said on the seventh of October that the country ordered 12 H225M multirole military helicopters. That is the latest dated order from the region. No Romanian space decision is on file, and no date is set. This is aviation, not space, so it carries low weight.

In Sweden, the national space agency announced on the second of November that its next Space Day is on the eighteenth of February, twenty twenty-seven. It is the next fixed Swedish space event.

In France, ArianeGroup said on the fourth of November that the second SyLEx sounding rocket launch succeeded. The M51 missile program is the related French defence work. In Spain, the International Telecommunication Union has accepted an extension for Open Cosmos but cut its broadband constellation by half. No next date is on file for either.

In Armenia, an Armath Engineering Makerspace has opened in Iraq. Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan have no new space decision on file. No date is set.

In Türkiye, a new microsatellite is slated for launch in 2028, and a joint satellite of Turkic states for 2027. The proposal of 24.59 billion lira for space and aviation in 2027 stands, with no split published. No decision date is on file.

In Indonesia, press accounts place the re-entry of NASA's Swift observatory over the west of the country on the fourth or fifth of November. One account names Sumatra. NASA has published no page, so the thread stays closed until it does. In South Korea, KT SAT will lead a maritime connectivity project with ST Engineering iDirect, announced on the fifth of November. In Japan, the MMX probe remains on its transfer orbit towards Mars, with no arrival date on file.

In Canada, Telesat has delayed full Lightspeed service to mid-2028. In the United States, NASA announced on the fourth of November Ka-band relay contracts for Viasat, SES and Astranis. Artemis dates are unchanged, and commercial station proposals are due on the eighth of December. Blue Origin's January return for New Glenn is reported and unconfirmed. The deadline for FAA comments passed on the thirtieth of October with no decision on file.

What we are tracking this week is the ESA committee vote on the tenth of November. This month, it is the Ariane 6 flight with 36 Amazon Leo satellites, no earlier than the twenty-third of November. The heads-up dates are the eighth of December for NASA station proposals, the fifteenth of December for Rome, and the eighteenth of February for Swedish Space Day. We are also watching for a NASA page on Swift, and for Blue Origin or the FAA to settle the New Glenn cadence. Several of these items are standing items without a fresh source in this reading, so we treat them as context rather than news. Dates are given as reported, and we will flag any change as soon as a primary source appears. That is the briefing for Sunday, the eighth of November.
